title: The tests' copy of the app's start-up leaves out six of its steps
what: The real-database tests start the app through a helper that says it does exactly what the app does when it opens. It does not: it skips the clean-up of photos whose workout is gone, the three one-time record fixes, the fix for imported workout times and the fix for folders copied from a Hevy link. No test opening the app on a real database ever runs these steps, so a change that breaks them at start-up would pass.
expected: The tests start the app through the same start-up the app uses, not a hand-kept copy.
fix_line: Make the test helper call the app's own start-up steps instead of its own list

title: The only tests of the Workout tab, import, exercise page, Body and photos pages look for words in the code
what: Every test that touches these screens reads the screen's code as text and looks for a line in it; none opens the screen. They pass even if the line is never reached, and fail on a harmless rename. One of them locks in a failure being swallowed: it checks that a failed demo-data check quietly counts as not-demo before Replace.
expected: Each of these screens has at least one test that opens it and checks what the member sees.
fix_line: Add one on-screen test per screen and drop the word-in-code checks it replaces

title: On the Workout tab, a failed plan read hides the plan's week line and easy-week offer without a word
what: When the followed plan or the count of stuck lifts cannot be read, the tab quietly treats it as no plan and no stuck lifts. The week line and the easy-week offer disappear, nothing says a read failed, nothing is logged, and unlike the other reads on this tab it is not tried again.
expected: A failed plan read is logged and tried again like the tab's other reads, and the plan line comes back once it reads.
fix_line: Mark the plan and stuck-lift reads as failed so the tab tries again, and log them

title: Pictures added on Add measures can stay on the wrong day without a word
what: When a member adds pictures and then changes the entry's day, saving moves the pictures to the new day. If that move fails, it is swallowed: the entry says saved and the pictures stay on the old day, with nothing shown or logged.
expected: A picture that could not be moved is logged and the member is told it stayed on the first day.
fix_line: Log the failed move and tell the member which pictures kept their old day

title: The list of old addresses and where they go is kept twice, and the test does not compare the two
what: Where each retired page sends people is written once in a shared list the app never reads, and again inside each old page. The test checks each old page redirects somewhere and that the list's target exists, but for most of them it never checks the page goes where the list says. An old page could send people to the wrong place and the test would pass.
expected: Old pages read their target from the one list, or the test checks each page's target equals the list.
how_often: every change to an old address
fix_line: Have each old page redirect to its entry in the shared list

title: The switched-off nutrition page is kept in the app with no test
what: The nutrition page (about 300 lines) is switched off and sends anyone who reaches it to the Workout tab. Its code is still built into the app, and no test opens it. Several of its reads turn a failure into an empty day with no message. It will need re-checking from scratch whenever it is switched on.
expected: Switched-off pages are either removed until their phase or kept with a test that opens them.
fix_line: Remove the page until its phase, or add one test that opens it

items.reason: no flaky-run record exists in the machine files; the tests touching these screens read code as text or use a real database with no timers, clocks or random values
